verdict.rationale: Kimi documents an official desktop app, Kimi Code Desktop, where the agent opens a local project folder to read and edit code, run commands, and verify results. The evidence says nothing about OS-level global shortcuts or screen awareness, which are core to this story. The browser extension is a different surface and earns no credit. Missing for 10: OS-level/global keyboard shortcuts, access to on-screen content or screen capture, a general-purpose desktop assistant beyond the coding workflow, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can use an official desktop app with OS-level shortcuts and access to what is on my screen

citations.quote: Open a local project folder in Kimi Code Desktop and let the Agent read code, edit files, run commands, and verify results through conversation.
